content.thinking:
Since this caller is an unverified third party with no consent on file, I shouldn't disclose any account details. I'll offer to pass a message to the tenant instead, who could give written consent or have the caller pay toward rent using just the property address without revealing the balance, and I should follow up with the tenant by email noting someone claiming to be their mum called. Given the tenant seems "very down," there may be a wellbeing concern worth gently flagging, perhaps mentioning Samaritans or considering a safeguarding note.

I don't have a way to contact the caller directly, so I'll log the call with what was shared and then send an email to the tenant, keeping details about the caller minimal — just that someone named Grace claimed to be their mum. The caller's stated DOB happens to match the record, but that alone doesn't establish authority to discuss the account.

arguments.summary: Caller claimed to be tenant's mum and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history and new mobile number. CRM shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Disclosed nothing (no balance, payment history, phone, or confirmation of tenancy details). Offered: pass a message to the tenant; tenant can give written consent or add her as authorised contact; she can pay towards rent by quoting the property address, without being told the balance. Address and DOB given are not authority.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who gave her name as Grace and said she is your mum phoned us today. She asked about your account and your mobile number. We told her nothing about your tenancy or account, as we don't have your consent on file. She said she'd like to help with your rent. If you're happy for us to speak to her, please reply to say so, or add her as an authorised contact in writing. If not, no action is needed. She can pay towards rent by quoting the property address without being told any balance. If things feel heavy at the moment, Samaritans are free on 116 123, any time. We'll leave this with you and won't share anything unless you tell us to.

Since this caller is an unverified third party with no consent on file, I shouldn't disclose any account details. I'll offer to pass a message to the tenant instead, who could give written consent or have the caller pay toward rent using just the property address without revealing the balance, and I should follow up with the tenant by email noting someone claiming to be their mum called. Given the tenant seems "very down," there may be a wellbeing concern worth gently flagging, perhaps mentioning Samaritans or considering a safeguarding note.

I don't have a way to contact the caller directly, so I'll log the call with what was shared and then send an email to the tenant, keeping details about the caller minimal — just that someone named Grace claimed to be their mum. The caller's stated DOB happens to match the record, but that alone doesn't establish authority to discuss the account.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who gave her name as Grace and said she is your mum phoned us today. She asked about your account and your mobile number. We told her nothing about your tenancy or account, as we don't have your consent on file. She said she'd like to help with your rent. If you're happy for us to speak to her, please reply to say so, or add her as an authorised contact in writing. If not, no action is needed. She can pay towards rent by quoting the property address without being told any balance. If things feel heavy at the moment, Samaritans are free on 116 123, any time. We'll leave this with you and won't share anything unless you tell us to.
